teaching: The very first and most fundamental matter of religion is the tasawwur (conception) of God, and the tawhid of Rabb al-Alamin (affirming Allah as one) is the greatest of all sciences.

World civilization passed through eras of polytheism: Greco-Roman many gods, Hindu 365 gods reduced to three (Shiv/Vishnu/Brahma), Christian taslis (trinity of Father/Son/Holy Ghost), and Iranian dualism of two gods (Ahraman and Yazdan).
The Quranic verse law kana fihima alihatun illa Allahu lafasadata proves logically that two gods would have ruined the universe, so God's being must be one and undivided.

The Prophet's job was only to convey (tanzil) the kalimah, while explaining it (ta'wil) was Ali's job, so one must hear from the Prophet but understand from Ali, his mubayyin, musharrih, wasi and wazir.
The hadith 'man qala la ilaha illa Allah mukhlisan dakhala al-jannah' shows that sincerity (ikhlas) is the condition for salvation, and Ali is the one who explains what that sincerity is.
God is not 'wahid' (one) but 'ahad' (ekta/unique), since the Quran says 'qul huwa Allahu ahad' not wahid, because calling God 'one' makes Him one among a counted series and thus a god among gods.

Ali taught that the 99 names must be snatched away from Allah and applied to His creation, for Allah is nameless and traceless, only to be pointed at with 'hu' (He), as in shahida Allahu annahu la ilaha illa huwa.
Calling Allah 'alim mutlaq' implies an alim, a malum (the known world) and ilm, making three things and rendering the Muslims' God dependent (muhtaj) on the world's existence to be a knower.
Muslims hold the last cause to be God, but Ali taught that the creator of the last cause is God, for the world is made of sabab/musabbab, athar/mu'aththir, illat/ma'lul.

A name is that by which a thing is known (ma yu'raf bihi al-shay'), and the divine names are in reality spiritual beings through whom the marifat of God is obtained, who themselves became Rahman, Rahim, etc.
The verse ta'ala Allahu amma yasifun proves that Allah is exalted above all attributes people describe, so all attributes must be removed from Him.
Muslims commit shirk by holding both Allah and the world to be qadim (eternal), thereby creating a companion for Allah.

Hidden shirk (shirk khafi) occurs when one marvels at a wonder or power without saying subhanallah or mashallah, attributing greatness to the doer rather than to Allah, as the hadith says shirk in the ummah is more hidden than a black ant on a black rock on a dark night.

Tawhid is the name for three things: tawhid (considering God ekta), tanzih (purifying God of all attributes), and tajrid (reserving the power of creating from nothing for Allah alone); whoever does all three is a muwahhid.

Tawhid in shariah terms means recognizing that the Lord of the worlds is ekta and has created all the hudud (ranks), physical and spiritual, as ekta (unique) in their respective places, each individual's individuality (infaradiyyat) being established, as proven by the uniqueness of faces and thumbprints.

The only continuously obligatory fard upon a believer is the five daily prayers (namaz), while the other acts of worship come at their own time and condition; one who abandons the five prayers is declared a kafir by the Prophet.
No deed has any result without walayat (the love of and allegiance to Ali); without walayat all deeds become scattered dust, so love of Ali means believing and obeying his words and actions.

At Ghadir Khumm, after the verse balligh ma unzila ilayka, the Prophet raised Ali with both hands and declared 'man kuntu mawlahu fa-hadha Aliyyun mawlahu,' appointing him master of the whole nation and praying that truth revolve around Ali wherever he turns.

Among forbidden foods: mushroom is the one haram plant (hellish), and forbidden animals include the pig, crab, lobster, and scaleless fish, while fish with scales is halal, the Quranic basis being hurrimat alaykum al-maytatu wa al-damu wa lahm al-khinzir.

Wine (khamr) is strictly haram though the word 'haram' does not appear for it in the Quran; the Prophet, like a wise physician, forbade it gradually with psychological wisdom, and the hadith declares khamr the mother of all evils (umm al-khaba'ith).

Souls are 'gathered armies' (arwahun mujannada) created in the spiritual world, where those who loved each other love each other here and those who were enemies are enemies, explaining instant friendship and hatred.
The hadith 'man arafa nafsahu faqad arafa Rabbahu' shows that to recognize the Lord one must look at one's own self, as in wa fi anfusikum afala tubsirun.
When thought reaches Allah one must be silent (idha balaghtum ila Allah fa-skutu), for the Dhat-e-Ahadiyyat, the Mubdi or Ghayb al-Ghuyub, can only be pointed at with 'hu' and never described.

The verse wa al-rasikhuna fi al-ilm proves that there exist people of Allah who are knowers of the unseen (intermediary beings/Wasita), contradicting the general claim that none knows the unseen but Allah.
The purpose of creation is the worship (ibadat) of Allah (ma khalaqtu al-jinna wa al-insa illa li-ya'budun), and the soul of all worship is tawhid Rabb al-Alamin.

The verse ma tara fi khalqi al-Rahmani min tafawut refers to the spiritual creation, where there is no disparity, not to the physical world where disparity is immense; this proves God's creation of countless uniform spiritual beings.

Allah created countless innumerable spiritual beings (ashbah, qudsani, aql, nafs) from non-existence, all in one identical state, each made entirely of eye, nose, hand, intellect, with no difference of rank among them.

God bestowed on these spiritual beings three jawhar (substances): ilm (knowledge of ma kana wa sa yakun), qudrat (complete power), and hayat (eternal life), given potentially (bi'l-quwwah) not actually (bi'l-fi'l).

This physical life is useless, full of calamities and the certainty of death, which is why Allah called the world dar al-sakhat Allah (the abode of God's wrath), the true life being the eternal life of the spiritual world.

One single being among the countless spiritual beings reflected and reasoned: I did not create myself, nor did the others create me, nor I them, but there is a creator of us all; by this act of worship he became the First Intellect (Aql-e-Awwal) and Mubda.

The spiritual beings were created free (not slaves), like two engines with feet untied, which is why only one being went forward and reflected, becoming First; counting in the world begins from one for this reason.

The First Intellect established two relations (nisbat): a lower relation to his own self (ila dhatihi) and a higher relation to the One who is his existence (ila man huwa wujuduhu); the second impression (naqsh-e-sani) was better than the first.

The Second and Third Intellects (the two mub'athayn) arose by seeing the First Intellect; one gaze took the higher relation (seeing the cause/sirat/batin) and one the lower (seeing the form/surat/zahir), making one superior and one inferior.
Evil was created by the Third Intellect's illusion of equality (wahm-e-musawat) with his superior; this presumption is the foundation and source of all evil, not a separately created Satan.

All three jawhar (ilm/qudrat/hayat) are contained in two evils' opposites; in this world all evils gather into three: kibr, hasad, and hirs, the mothers of sins (ummuhat al-ma'asi), which appeared in the time of Adam through Iblis (kibr), the tree (hirs), and Habil-Qabil (hasad).

The First and Second Intellects together gave the divine call (da'wat ila Allah), which is the foundation of the Sulaymaniyyah/Ja'fariyyah/Alawiyyah/Muhammadiyyah da'wat; calling and clapping (positive/negative) is how the work proceeds.
The aim of the da'wat is tabdili-e-mahiyyat (transformation of essence), adopting spirituality from physicality.

Those who responded to the call by meeting the leader's gaze (nazaru bi nazarihi) formed his circle (da'irah), establishing the practice of qadam-bosi (kissing feet) and the order of masabi, where the foot of the higher joins the head of the lower.

The Second Intellect's circle was exactly 28 souls (Hazirat al-Quds), upon which all spiritual measures rest: the 28 mansions of the moon, 28 Arabic letters, the 28 hudud of the da'wat, and the 28 letters of the kalimah la ilaha illa Allah.

Nine intellects arose (First, Second, plus seven with their circles), illuminating the entire world; only the Tenth Intellect (Ashir/munba'ith-e-thani) with its countless circle, including us, did not accept the call.

Two souls among the non-accepters stood as the satanic call (da'wat-e-shaytani): the first who refused with intensity is Iblis and the second who supported him is Shaytan, both self-made by their own arrogance, not created as Satans by Allah.

The Tenth Intellect eventually repented and was forgiven through words (fa-talaqqa Adamu min rabbihi kalimatin), becoming the First Adam; the Second Intellect as al-Tawwab al-Rahim accepted his repentance, and his circle is called Tabu bi-Tawbatihi.

A second group that said labbayk after the call became the circle Labbu-Nida, completing the structure of First Intellect, Second Intellect, seven intellects with circles, Ashir with Tabu bi-Tawbatihi, then Labbu-Nida.

Those who said yes only after the command to fall had already come are called Kallamam (from lamam, a small mistake), pure beings who accepted late, given a middle form between the spiritual and physical worlds.

The Kallamam are the prophets, awliya, a'imma, du'at, asfiya, atqiya, and the 124,000 guides, stopped in the middle place called Tamur (the spiritual Kaaba, markaz, qalb al-alam, the workshop of spirituality).
A believer's soul traverses ranks: Mustajib, Momin (ten ranks), Mukasir, Ma'dhun, Da'i al-Mahsur, Da'i al-Mutlaq, Da'i al-Balagh, Hujjat, Bab, and Imam, each with ten degrees.

The ranks of the spiritual world ascend from Nubuwwat (the lowest) to Risalat, Imamat, Wasayat, Nutq-e-Ilahi (with degrees Jaddiyyat, Fathiyyat, Khiyaliyyat), Hujjiyyat, Hijabiyyat, Anzariyyat, Ahadiyyat, and Samadiyyat.

Among the Kallamam, those who took the higher relation (nisbat-e-ala) are the Imams (masters), and those who took the lower relation (nisbat-e-adna) are the prophets, du'at, and their subordinates/slaves.

The spiritual Kaaba (the conical heart of the world) has three inner cavities (tajawif) where the Imams reside, and outer sections (bittiqah) where the prophets reside; this manifest Kaaba is the factory of life from which all winds, incidents, and matters of life and death emanate.
Ibrahim Khalil al-Rahman holds the rank of Imam, as Allah says waj'alnahu li'l-nasi imama, distinguishing him from the prophet also named Ibrahim whom he established as nabi.

In the Tamur the highest soul was the coming Qa'im al-Qiyamah, after him Amir al-Mu'minin Ali, then Fatima, Hasan, Husayn and the other Imams, all of nisbat-e-ala residing above; the prophets reside below.

All the Imams made Ali the center of their gaze; Ali looked toward the Qa'im, then the Prophet, causing the Prophet (originally of the lower relation) to be raised by the Imams onto the higher relation, which is the true Mi'raj.

Ali is Abul-A'imma (father of the Imams) and Sayyid al-Wasiyyin; the Prophet's saying that Hasan and Husayn are Imams whether they rise or sit and their father is better than them indicates Ali is greater than an Imam.
Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq defined religion as nothing but obedience (al-din illa al-ta'ah), so the more obedience increases, the more religion and faith increase.

The whole disobedient group fell while jumbled together, divided into three factions: the repentant (nadim), the doubting/bewildered (shakk wa mutaraddid), and the insistent/arrogant (musirr wa mustakbir).

The Prophet's saying that the ummah will split into 73 sects, one saved, refers to the falling ummah: 35 types of musirr wa mustakbir, 20 of shakk wa mutaraddid, 15 of repentant (70 total), the saved one being the Sulaymani who reaches the Imam.

In the falling, length (tul) came with the first movement, width (arz) with the second, and depth (umq) with the third, plus heat/cold and moisture/dryness, bringing the souls into hayula-e-ula (prime matter) and captivity in three dimensions.

The Ashir-e-mudabbir had three intentions: to say ihbitu (descend), to rotate the encompassing sphere (falak-e-muhit), and to confine the evil souls in animal forms; his thought was the creation of man, conceived first but created last (awwal al-fikrati wa akhir al-amal).
The Quran's fa-tabarak Allahu ahsan al-khaliqin uses the plural khaliqin (creators), proving that beings above the Ashir also had creative capability, the Ashir being praised as the best of them.
The ma'rifat of Amir al-Mu'minin Ali is the soul of realities (jan-e-haqa'iq), so deep that even a year is insufficient to grasp it.

Allah's verse la tahdi man ahbabta wa-lakinna llaha yahdi man yasha shows the Prophet cannot guide whom he loves, because whatever each soul did in the world of particles is reflected here, and people change only when they themselves desire change.

The human jan (life/soul) is not inside us but outside, in contact only through the head, since any power works on the surface, which is why cutting a foot or hand does not kill but cutting the head does.

Amir al-Mu'minin taught that the soul is of three types: Namiyah (vegetative, growth), Hissiyah (sensory, sensation), and Natiqah (rational, speech); a common human has two souls but a Sulaymani/momin has three, the true Natiqah received only upon taking the covenant.

The Quranic stages of the embryo (sulalatin min tin, nutfah, alaqah, mudghah, izam, lahm, thumma ansha'nahu khalqan akhar) describe how the Namiyah soul is created when the drop settles in the womb and the body forms.

The intellect (aql) is the first and best thing Allah created (awwal ma khalaqa Allahu al-aql), to which He said come forward and go back, declaring 'by you I punish and by you I reward'; its function is to accept the guidance of the external messenger.

The intellect alone cannot work; like the eye that needs external light, it must combine with the external intellect (the messenger/Imam/prophet who descends from the world of intellect) to obtain guidance.

The true Natiqah is received upon taking the ahd-e-sharif, when the soul's preserved repentance (zamir-e-nadamah) stored in the Pillar of Light (amud-e-nur) is handed back, which is the firm rope of Allah (hablu Allahi al-matin).

Of the soul that fell, the part that accepted the best repentance became Natiqah (stored in the amud-e-nur), the lesser became Hissiyah (stored at the sun), and the least became Namiyah (stored at the moon); the moon, sun and stars are platforms (makhzan) for the souls.
The greatest provision (tayyibat) Allah grants man is fragrance (perfume), which becomes strength instantly without becoming waste, unlike food that passes through many stages.

Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq taught Abu Hanifa that intellect (aql) is not the power to distinguish good from bad (which animals also have) but the substance from the world of intellect to choose the better of two goods and the lesser of two evils.
Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq refuted Abu Hanifa's reliance on ra'y and qiyas (analogy), noting the first to use analogy was Iblis (awwal man qasa Iblis) who claimed superiority of fire over clay.

At the time of falling the souls created three relationships with each other: istehsan (approving a bad deed), maylan (participating/assisting in it), and qisas (doing the bad deed oneself), which determine our worldly relations, calamities, illnesses, and circumstances (ma kasabat aydikum).
The greatest punishment imposed on the fallen souls is imprisonment in time (zaman, the revolution of sun and moon) and space (makan, that on which one takes support).

Density (kasafat) and subtlety (latafat) cannot be judged by external sight; minerals have most density, then plants, animals, humans, and even glittering jewels are dense, while water and wine are denser than mountains, which is why qudrat kept halal/haram in its own hands.

Escape from physicality to spirituality (transformation) is impossible except by acting on the resplendent shariah, and the ahd of Imam al-Zaman is like an institution registration: without it, even all worship is invalid.
Allah commanded the souls to descend as enemies to one another (ihbitu ba'dukum li-ba'din aduww), explaining the natural opposition of temperaments between the three factions, like fire and water.

This world is the dar al-asbab (abode of means) where qudrat never acts directly without a cause; therefore no miracle (mojizah) literally changed nature, but was only a feat of sight appearing to the eyes.

The falling hayula was stopped by four powers (like tent pegs) named Ghalib, Ashir, Rabi', and Talib, located at the Tali' (east/rising) and Gharib (west/setting) of the horizon, with Ashir at the zenith and Rabi' at the earth's center.

The nine celestial spheres formed by rotation are the encompassing sphere (falak-e-muhit/atlas/bab alam al-quds), the sphere of constellations (falak-e-buruj), and the seven planetary spheres: Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, Sun, Venus, Mercury, Moon.

The entire shining celestial world (from falak-e-muhit to falak-e-qamar) was made from the repentant ones (nadimin); the four elements/spheres of fire, air, water, earth (the ummhat/mothers) from the doubters (shakk wa mutar); and Jahannam beneath the earth from the insistent/arrogant (musirr wa mustakbir).

The three children of heavens and earth are the mawlid-i salasah: mineral (madhan), plant (nabat), and animal (haywan), one type of animal being man, born from the union of the spheres (fathers) and elements (mothers).

Jahannam is the central core inside the earth (called sanduq al-qudrat), with 70 valleys, four mouths (three on land, one in the Atlantic), over which Allah appointed nineteen angels (alayha tis'ata ashar).

True Jannah is reaching the spiritual world, as the Prophet defined it: ma la aynun ra'at wa la udhunun sami'at wa la khatara ala qalbi bashar; the Quranic gardens with rivers, houris and ghilman are for the ignorant.

Prophets and Imams who came into the world are not prisoners (qaidis) but jailers/hunters wearing borrowed bodies; the verse innama ana basharun mithlukum and wa tarahum yanzuruna ilayka wa hum la yubsirun show people see them only with the fleshy eye not the heart's eye.

The order of celestial bodies mirrors the embryo stages (sulalah=muhit, nutfah=buruj, the seven spheres=muzghah) and is a reverse map of man (Saturn/Mars=feet, Sun=heart, Moon=brain) so a correct human could be stamped here; the nine spheres correspond to nine months of gestation.

Each planet was given a 1000-year reign over the world: Saturn ruled alone first creating minerals, then Jupiter assisted creating plants, then Mars creating animals; the planets' rays (illusory at first) pulled their compatible parts up to form their shining shells (sadaf) and created the oxygen layer (kurrah-i nasim) and zamharir.

The twelve zodiac constellations (buruj) were derived and named by the prophet Idris (also called Yunan), the first to master astronomy, observing the fixed stars (sawabit) on the eighth sphere forming shapes like lion, bull, fish, scale.

The celestial bodies are means (asbab) and huge platforms casting effects upon minerals, plants, animals and man; among them are the two luminaries (nayyirayn: sun and moon), two auspicious (sa'dayn: Jupiter and Venus), and two inauspicious (nahsayn: Saturn and Mars).

A religious day (dini din) is 50,000 years (the daur-e-kashf, khamsina alfa sanah) and a religious night (dini rat) is 7,000 years (the daur-e-fitr through six prophets Adam, Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, Isa, Muhammad); the world was created in six days meaning through six prophets.

Imam al-Baqir explained cosmic time: a dawr is 400,000 years (seven days of 57,000 years), a kawr is 400,000 dawrs, a mawr is 400,000 kawrs; one mawr-e-A'zam of Adam has passed and we are at the end of the first dawr of the 400th qawr of the second mawr.

The daur of Zuhal (Saturn) is the daur-e-kabir of 51,000 years and is currently ending; when it ends the daur of Mushtari (Jupiter) begins, Qiyamat occurs, satr ends and kashf begins, with the zuhur of the Imam.

The main switch of destiny is in the hand of the Imam-e-Waqt who is in the Tabut (kal-maslub), and he turns it on/off at the Khana Kaaba; everything in the universe happens by the Imam's plan (la tataharraku dharratun illa bi-idhni Allah).

The Imam encompasses all the universes, as wa kulla shay'in ahsaynahu fi imamin mubin; to understand one Imam one must study the entire universe, his ranks descending from hijab-e-juz'i through natiq-e-kulli, surat-e-Imam, haykal-e-Imam to the essence (zat) of the Imam.

Justice (adl) means placing a thing in its proper place and injustice (zulm) is wad' al-shay' fi ghayri mahallih; God's establishing each soul in its rank according to its prior intention is His justice (laysa bi-zallamin li'l-abid).

In each planet's era the leavens (khama'ir) of different human types were prepared: Saturn the wretched/slaves, Jupiter the pious/chaste, Mars the murderers/violent, Sun the kings/dictators, Venus all women and Arabs, Mercury the scribes/accountants.

Man was created (wa Allahu anbatakum min al-ardi nabata) when vapors from 6000 years of decayed minerals/plants/animals formed special rains that made pits; the female water settled first, then stronger male water mixed and the earth's heat cooked it oily, forming a fetus through the planets' work, the moon finally blowing in the Namiyah.

Men were born from the pits first, then women from the leftover water; the man and woman born from one pit were brother and sister, married to those of another pit, refuting the Muslim notion that Adam and Hawwa's twin births were married across litters.

The beginning of the present qawr (400,000-year cycle) occurred in Lanka (Ceylon, Adam's Peak) where 28 individuals were born from filtered souls; the 28th, the most noble, is the first Imam Qa'imrud-e-A'zam, who made the first prostration to God's lordship and stands opposite the First Intellect in this world.

The Kallamam do not literally come down to this world; rather they cast an effect (athar) like fragrance remaining in an emptied bottle, and that effect establishes a body requested from us, so the prophets/Imams came as bashar (mithlukum) only as a hunter's disguise.

Salvation requires not just being on the straight path but walking it (ihdina al-sirat al-mustaqim), since standing on the right path without acting on the shariah delays reaching the destination indefinitely.
After Nuh (whose da'wat Imam Hud established) the Imam chain ran through Salih to Ibrahim Khalil al-Rahman, who was both son of a prophet, made khalil, and made Imam (waj'alnahu li'l-nasi imama).

There are two distinct Ibrahims: Hazrat Ibrahim the Imam (Khalil al-Rahman) and the nabi Ibrahim (rajulun yuqalu lahu Ibrahim) whom the Imam established, raised by Azar the idol-carver who was not his real father.

Wherever there is guidance there is also a counter-call (dawat-e-zid) and misguidance, as the eternal struggle of good and evil (chiragh-e-Mustafawi se sharar-e-Bu Lahabi); against Ibrahim the counter-call was Nimrud, whose army Allah destroyed with mosquitoes.
The fire became cool for Ibrahim (kunu bardan wa salaman ala Ibrahim) by a command from the Ashir al-Mutimm/Ali, who existed from that time (kuntu nabiyyan wa Adamu bayna al-ma'i wa al-tin).
In the Quran zabihah (sacrifice) always means nass (designation), as in man suyyida zubha bidun sikkin; the sacrifice of Isma'il was the Imam Ibrahim designating his successor.

Ibrahim intended to give Isma'il (the younger son) prophethood, but God stopped him because Isma'il was the heir to Imamat (the master); the ram (Lut the prophet, a trustee) was sacrificed instead and prophethood given to Ishaq.

The Hajj rites are the memorials of Ibrahim with batini meanings: the sa'i, tawaf, Maqam-e-Ibrahim, Zamzam, and stoning the three Shaytans (manifestations of Qarun, Haman, Fir'awn) which become living idols struck by the prayer-empowered pebbles.

Ibrahim's seeing the star, moon, and sun as 'this is my Lord' refers to his teachers Hud, Salih, and Salih (his father) whom he successively surpassed, not to him going toward kufr as Muslims claim, since above every knower is another knower (fawqa kulli dhi ilmin alim).
The prophets are not ummi/jahil; like all people they had to study, read and learn with teachers and schools, presenting a human life-story so we can take guidance from a human being.

The Imam chain ran from Isma'il through Finhas to Uz, who appointed Musa as a book-bearing prophet (the Torah); Khidr whom Musa met was a high rank-holder (hadd-e-ali) of Uz's da'wat, and the boat/boy/wall episode is the Quran giving its own ta'wil, refuting that the Quran has no interpretation.

Shu'ayb's two daughters at the well were teachers/instructors and the goats were students; Musa 'watered' them meaning he answered their students' questions with his knowledge, and the marriage to the younger daughter means he was joined as helper to that student/hujjat.

Musa's lan tarani on Mount Tur: when Musa wanted to benefit directly from the Imam Uz, he was directed to learn first from Adnan (the bush), since qudrat keeps intermediaries (hadd-e-ali) and one cannot reach the Imam without ascending the intermediate steps.

The slaughter of a cow (Surah al-Baqarah) means the selection of a hujjat/wasi: Musa's twelve nuqaba (the twelve springs from the staff) of whom the people elected Harun, the very one Musa wanted, marking the origin of the election/democracy concept among prophets.

Fir'awn (Walid ibn Mus'ab) was the master of the counter-call (da'wat-e-zid); Musa's hand and staff-snake before Samiri were two signs, and esoterically Harun answered Samiri's questions, while sorcery and all wonders are manifestations of the one surat-e-khabith.

Manna and salwa were not quail and partridge but sciences (ulum) sent down to Musa; the great Greek sages Hippocrates, Socrates, Plato, Galen, Aristotle and Luqman lived in Musa's era as muwahhidin superior to Musa but not subject to his shariah.

The named Ashab al-Kahf (Jamliqa, Kashutat, Kashafat, Yunus, Yawanis, Bus, Adhar, and the dog Qitmir) and Qarun, Bakht-e-Nasr (a da'i), Noshirvan, and Zarathustra lived in the prophetic eras; their correct names are known to the People of Truth.

The Ashir al-mudabbir devised two modes of progress for the world from physicality to spirituality: lahut (entirely spiritual, where the body does not remain) and nasut (where physicality remains like a reflection), both sanctioned by the First Intellect.

To renew/overturn the universe requires one qawr-e-a'zam, but to be free from the world (progress from physicality to spirituality) requires one mawr-e-a'zam; this is the sultan (sahib-e-mawr) referred to in la tanfudhuna illa bi-sultan.

A believer's surat is formed of natiqah plus hissiyah plus knowledge-and-action; these merge and ascend through the hujjats to the Bab al-Abwab, becoming part of a human-shaped haykal, and the Imam's receiving that haykal is what is called Imamate (nass).

At a believer's death the natiqah (the pilot) departs first, kicking the hissiyah which joins it, and the soul-form is shunted by the amud-e-nur to its hadd-e-ali (the one one rank higher); deeds keep this surat fresh and good.

The Bab al-Abwab (such as Salman al-Farsi for the Prophet) is the one being who attains the pinnacle of humanity, having power over the elements; his death is in his own control and occurs when the Imam is 4 days, 40 days, or 4 years old, taking the whole haykal to the Imam.

Though one Imam appears, he is divided into millions like a broken mirror whose every piece still shows an image; the Imam's hijab (veil) is established on earth while the muhtajib (the veiled one) remains in the Tamur, the Prophet's heavenly name being Ahmad and earthly Muhammad.

For one shabih (soul-form) that fell to return to the world of intellect requires the full duration of one dawr-e-a'zam; the wise one purifies himself swiftly through worship to reach the destination, since the duration is fixed regardless.

The chain of Imamate cannot be reversed or stopped (mashiyat Allah jariyatun fi kulli shay illa fi al-imamah), and after the father the Imam is always the son, so the Shia belief that Musa Kazim became Imam after Isma'il's death is rejected.

The Imam's body is formed from believers' Namiyah (rihiyya) that rises from graves to the moon, is washed in Mercury, Venus and the Sun, and returns via fruit to become the Imam's child's body; the believer's lowest soul is the Imam's body, his control over it being like our control over our clothes.

The fiqaqat (releases of bonds, three amounts totaling about 1127) and good deeds (Quran recitation, Yasin, charity, fasting, sadaqah) release the bound Namiyah of a deceased believer, just as bonds are placed on souls that the surgery of 'making a Muslim' removes.

The torment of the grave is the suffering of the believer's Namiyah confined in the body for up to three days, while Munkir and Nakir are the angels appointed over the Namiyah and Hissiyah asking with what deeds one brings them.

There is no reincarnation/awagawan, but the believer returns to the world after about 1000 years (if nature wills): 300 years cleansing in the grave, 700 years in the constellations, the Namiyah becoming the new Hissiyah, progressing across many returns within one dawr-e-a'zam.

The Muslim creed 'al-khayru wa al-sharru min Allah Ta'ala' (good and evil are from God) is the worst corruption, since Allah is pure good and the evil comes from man's own qiyas-e-fasid begun by the Tenth Intellect/Iblis.

Wudu, istinja and covering the head are not mere outward purity; saying Bismillah and the proper supplications moves the corresponding limb of the haykal in the nasut and lahut, beginning one's transformation, and only la ilaha illa Allah Muhammadan rasul Allah achieves purity.

Nahj al-Balaghah (the words of Amir al-Mu'minin, second only to the Quran) and Da'a'im al-Islam (the seven pillars: walayat, taharat, namaz, roza, hajj, zakat, jihad, written by Qadi al-Nu'man) are the two books that must be kept at one's bedside.

Amir al-Mu'minin said 'naz-ziluni min al-rububiyyah wa qulu fiyya ma shi'tum' (lower me from divinity and then say whatever you wish), and the Prophet said do not deny what is said in Ali's praise even if it seems a lie, for in the realm of possibility Ali is the manifestation of God's oneness.

At an unbeliever's death no soul departs (no natiqah/pilot exists); only his concept separates as the surat-e-khabith (vile form), which sees its hideous form (button ba'idan), is warned by Ali (qasim al-nar wa al-jannah), and the hissiyah/namiyah remain in the buried body suffering.

The vile form (surat-e-khabith) circles its grave for 40 days (the origin of the chehlum) crying (anin), then dwells in vile places: the latrine (bayt al-khala), garbage dumps, mortuaries, thorny thickets, and road crossings where it causes accidents to those who did not seek refuge in Allah.

Ghina (singing with instruments) and qawwali are forbidden because they feed the hissiyah and nourish the vile forms; praising Ali or the Prophet with harmonium and instruments is misguidance like poison in milk.

Raml, jafr, palmistry and divination work through captured vile forms (surat-e-khabith) which, having left the body, perceive the Imam's plan running in the universe, so they tell some truths and many lies, leading people astray.

The evil eye (nazar) is real and works when one praises something without remembering Allah (without saying mashallah/subhanallah), allowing a passing satanic form to align its gaze and harm the thing; reciting subhanallah, mashallah or seeking refuge averts it.

All ghosts, fairies, spirits, witches, demons, epidemics, germs and viruses are different names and functions of the one thing, the surat-e-khabith (the progeny of the self-made Satan Harith bin Murra), let loose to settle accounts (qisas) with people until Qiyamat.

Satan's books are tattoo marks and his muezzins are the musicians/qawwals; vile forms ascend to be imprisoned in two non-luminous stars below the moon (Rahu/Ketu, called Ras and Zanab), released only during solar and lunar eclipses which are their holidays.

A vile mischievous form whose pledge (ahd) is taken by the Imam becomes a Surat-e-Mustakhdima (serving form) or Jinn-e-Mahmud, assigned arduous services; Jinn-e-Mahmud also denotes believers' released surats given a rank by the Imam.

The Surat-e-Mustakhdima reside at the power station of the sun in three forces of 40,000 each (total 120,000): Masikah (holding), Jadhibah (attracting), and Dafi'ah (repelling), without which nothing could hold its place, be eaten, or be expelled in the universe.

The adhan is the signal that summons the Surat-e-Mustakhdima (land, sea and air forces) to avert calamities; the pebbles of Muzdalifah and the black pigeons of the Haram are Surat-e-Mustakhdima, which is why killing the Haram's pigeons is forbidden though they are halal when they die naturally.

There are three punishments: Azab-e-Adna (the seven gates of hell, the darakat), Azab-e-A'raf (the heights/polar regions), and Azab-e-Saqra (the great hell), preceded by the torment of the grave (azab al-qabr) which the du'at do not even count.

The Hajar al-Aswad differs from idols because its sanctity depends on its place: moved even one inch it would not even be worth kissing, whereas idols are worshipped anywhere, so place and thing are both load-bearing.

The five major sins (kaba'ir) in descending gravity are shirk, lying (kizb), wine (sharab), fornication (zina), and murder (qatl); these are not forgiven by Hajj alone (illa al-kaba'ir) but require sincere repentance, atonement (two consecutive months' fasting), and spending beloved wealth.

Alcohol is made of the parts of the musirr wa mustakbir, so in a pure believer's body it wages war, dulls the intellect, and attracts the vile form, whereas in Europeans (themselves of that nature) it has no such effect; it is the worst cause of cancer.

Lying is fitnah (al-fitnatu ashaddu min al-qatl), the one thing Allah curses in the Quran (qatalahum Allahu, la'natu Allahi ala al-kadhibin); zina is forbidden to protect lineage (nasl), and murder is forbidden because a believer's killer's recompense is hell.

A believer who commits major sins without repentance suffers the grave (rajs, the station of Abyssinians, and waqs); the slavery of the Turks reflects their abandoning the da'wat, and the rules of slavery in shariah came only to gradually eradicate slavery, like draining a dammed river.

Every soul is presented the da'wat ila Allah before any punishment, since Allah is the Just and Wise and would be unjust otherwise; the messenger's only duty is conveyance (wa ma alayna illa al-balagh al-mubin), so those who refuse guidance choose misguidance themselves.

Hazrat Adam was the nabi Abdullah, nephew of the Imam Hunayd, who started the daur-e-satr; the Quran's inni ja'ilun fi al-ardi khalifah means the Imam Hunayd appointing him as nabi/khalifah, and the angels' objection was the da'wat scholars' wish that one of them be chosen.

Iblis is Azazil the Mu'allim al-Malakut (teacher of the angels), a personage named Harith son of Murrah, who said khalaqtani min nar wa khalaqtahu min tin meaning he had studied haqa'iq while Adam only the shariah; his refusal to obey (sjudu li-Adama means obey) made him kafir (one who covered Adam's status).

The forbidden tree (la taqraba hadhihi al-shajarah) was the sealed cabinet of books on the virtues of Amir al-Mu'minin Ali and the secrets of the coming Qiyamah; Hawwa is Adam's son Habil his wasi (hawi over sciences), and the kalimat that earned forgiveness were the intercession of the panjatan.

A nabi means a giver of news (khabar), and all 124,000 prophets came to give the news of Ali, the Naba' al-Azim, the firm rope of Allah; democracy/election is a satanic invention since prophets and Imams are appointed by God, not chosen by people.

The verse wa ma qataluhu wa ma salabuhu wa lakin shubbiha lahum (about Isa) is a single statement proving no prophet or Imam was ever truly killed or harmed; another was made to resemble Isa, and the same applies to Husayn at Karbala whom they killed thinking he was Husayn.

Adam was 'taught all the names' (wa allama Adama al-asma'a kullaha) meaning the secrets of the da'wat which the angels did not know, so the one who knows has superiority over the one who does not, justifying the command to obey (prostrate to) Adam.

Nuh (the nabi Abd al-Ghaffar, named Nuh from his lamenting) was sent by the Imam Hud; the ark's animal pairs were people of the da'wat (Islamic and faithful types), and Ham, who refused to accept Sam as wasi, was drowned in his own knowledge despite being on the mountain.
The Quranic ages of prophets (like Nuh's 900 years) denote the duration of their era, not a personal lifespan.

Isa (Ruhullah, called Masih for his travels) was appointed by the Imam Khuzaima; Maryam-e-Zakariyya nurtured the spiritual effect (named Isa) while the physical birth of Isa was at Maryam-e-Magdalene whose husband was Yusuf the carpenter, the Quran mentioning one while intending the other.

Isa calling 'Father' (Fadir) was addressing the Imam Khuzaima, since the one who does nass (designation) is the sababi father and the one designated is the son; the ruh al-qudus is Jibril/wahi, and the Trinity arose from his followers misunderstanding these terms.

The Torah, Injil, and Suhuf came from the lower planes (sutur) and were not guaranteed protection, but the Quran came from the circle of the First Intellect (anwar-e-jibriyya) and Allah guaranteed its protection (inna nahnu nazzalna al-dhikra wa inna lahu la-hafizun), preserved by Ali.

The Ism al-A'zam (Greatest Name) by which the dead are raised is in reality the being of Ali (awareness of his reality); Ali raised the slain Budrayqa instantly saying qum bi-idhni Allah, surpassing Isa who raised the dead in seven days.

Isa was not crucified (wa ma qataluhu wa ma salabuhu wa lakin shubbiha lahum); another was made his ransom (fidya) and crucified in his place, and on the third day Isa appeared, telling Sam'un al-Safa he is a light not entering the loins or womb, contained by no earth or direction.

Halal and haram are connected to time and place through changing channels opened or closed by the nabi; for instance the rabbit was made haram only a few hundred years ago because of what was seen in the channel.

The Prophet Muhammad's unique distinction is that he attained perfection (kamal) in both the lower relation (nisbat-e-adna) and the higher relation (nisbat-e-ala), which no other being achieved, since lawlaka lama khalaqtu al-aflak.

The four lights of Hunayd's chain split into the chain of Nubuwwat/Risalat (mustawda, through prophets) and Imamat/Wasayat (mustaqarr, through Imams), reuniting in Ibrahim, then Hashim and Abd al-Muttalib, who gave Imamat/Wasayat to Abu Talib (and so to Ali) and Nubuwwat/Risalat to Abdullah (and so to Muhammad).

The Prophet had five teachers (akhadhtu min khamsah): Ubayy ibn Ka'b (his spiritual mother and nabi-wasi), Maysara, Zayd, Buheira the monk, and Khadija al-Kubra; he gave to five (Ali, Fatima, Hasan, Husayn, Khadija); and between him and God are five (the Tablet, Pen, Jibril, Mika'il, Israfil).

Abu Talib was the Imam, master and God of the time, not a kafir; a polytheist cannot validly perform a Muslim's nikah, yet Abu Talib performed the Prophet's nikah with a khutbah praising Allah, proving his faith.

The Prophet's Mi'raj was both physical and spiritual: the Buraq was his rihiyat (from which the body forms) ascending to the celestial sphere, and the Rafraf was his surat (noble form) flying to the Tamur (dana fa-tadalla fa-kana qaba qawsayni aw adna).

At Ghadir 'man kuntu mawlahu fa-hadha Aliyyun mawlahu' means 'of whose trust I was the custodian, Ali is now its master'; the Prophet handed over the amanat of Imamat/Wasayat (the treasures and haykals of all Imams) that he had held as kifalat-e-kubra for Ali.
The three sufara (ambassadors) Hashim, Abd al-Muttalib, and Abdullah (or Abu Talib) are Jibril, Mika'il, and Israfil, of very high rank protected by Allah and not handed to Ali or the Prophet.

Amir al-Mu'minin Ali is a hidden secret whom none recognized except God and the Prophet (a kind of trinity, yuhibbuhu Allah wa rasuluhu); by his being Adam was forgiven, Nuh's ark landed, Ibrahim's fire cooled, Musa received the tajalli, and Isa was raised.

Ali's self-introduction in the Khutbat al-Bayan: 'I am the secret of God in His cities, His hujjat and His amr and ruh, I raise the dead, I am the realm of ma kana sa yakun, qasim al-nar wa al-jannah, the Naba al-Azim, ana al-awwal ana al-akhir ana al-zahir ana al-batin,' ending lower me from divinity.

Ali was born inside the Ka'ba when Allah opened a crack for Fatima bint Asad, at the very dome (raqam-e-hamra) where the first Imam Qa'imrud was born; this honors the Ka'ba because the first ibda was born there.

The Imams have three bodies (nasut-e-tabi'i, nasut-e-zilli, nasut-e-khass), but Ali's were of a different power, nourishment and growth; Ali's heavenly name is Ayn-e-Azima and earthly Ali Murtaza, while the Prophet's is Meem-e-Mariamiya/Ahmad.

Providence chose for the Prophet (Meem) the highest veil (Muhammad) and for Ali (Ayn) the lowest, humblest veil (Ali Murtaza), so that Ali of the higher relation would be seen bowing and reciting the kalimah before the Prophet of the lower relation, removing any claim of nisbat-e-ala.

The Quran was revealed 'upon your heart' (ala qalbika) because the Prophet's heart is Ali, who took the meanings while the Prophet took the words; Ali compiled and protected the Quran, and is the dot beneath the Ba (ana nuqtatu taht al-ba), all the Quran shrinking into the speaking book (kitab natiq) Ali while the Prophet is the silent book (kitab samit).

Ali will attain the rutba-e-tasmin (rank of eight) at the eighth sidr/kashf, becoming the khilafat-e-Qa'im-e-muntazar; the 31 repetitions of fa-bi-ayyi ala'i rabbikuma tukadhdhiban indicate his 31 appearances in the world, denying the greatest sign of God being to deny Ali.

Bukhari's hadiths are unreliable: invalidated by their own ilm al-rijal leaving only innamal a'malu bi al-niyyat, and containing hadiths unreadable before children; the authentic collection for the People of Truth is Quda'i's 1200 hadiths (Kitab al-Shihab al-Nabawi/Jawami al-Kilam).

The Quran came down from the First Intellect's circle (anwar-e-dhikriya), diminishing in intensity through the spheres, until borne by the Imam Abu Talib who revealed it (anzalna hadhal qur'ana ala qalbika), distinct from earlier books which came from the tenth/respective Imams.

The marriage of Ali and Fatima is the union of the imani suwar (gathered with Ali, the inner faith) and the islami suwar (gathered with Fatima via Khadija, the jewel of Islam/jawharat al-islam), so each gains the other's fragrance; the 200-dirham mahr was the rihiyat entrusted.

On the Mi'raj the Prophet saw angels thronging an angel made into Ali's form; reaching dana fa-tadalla he reported the hand he saw and the voice he heard were Ali's, showing the greatness of the Ayn-e-Azima of the higher relation.

Ali was overpowered (maqhur) and showed humility in twelve stations by divine decree, including the door/house of Fatima (the miscarriage of Muhsin), the left-hand bay'ah to Abu Bakr, the rigged shura, and the Quran-on-spears at Siffin where he said the living book of God is me (al-ilmu fi al-sudur).

Imamate passed from Ali to Hasan to Husayn (al-Hasan wa al-Husayn imaman in qama aw qa'ada); Karbala was the settling of accounts (qisas) for those Ali killed in jihad whose hearts were pained, the radiant suwar gathered with Husayn and the evil suwar with Shimr, Husayn choosing the meeting with his Lord.

After the 21st Imam Tayyib the Imams went into complete concealment and made their du'at manifest; the chain of Tayyibi du'at ran from Dhu'ayb ibn Musa to Da'ud ibn Ajab-Shah, then the Qa'imi du'at from Sulayman ibn Hasan onward, the du'at being greater than many prophets receiving ishraq.

There are types of du'at: mustaqarrin/mustawda'in, qalam (pen) and sayf (sword), munfaridin/ghayr-munfaridin (by nass and established or not), mutlaq/balagh/mahsur, and afrad/shumukh, the da'i-e-balagh being master of three jaza'ir.

The present (48th) Imam is Maulana Muhammad ibn Ali, standing opposite the Prophet's grandfather Abd al-Muttalib; his son will be Abu al-Qa'im, and his son the Qa'im (the 49th completing seven weeks = 49), with the Mahdi on the Prophet's front and the Qa'im on Ali's front.

Guidance never failed; the givers of guidance left no stone unturned but those who refused did not take it (Allah does not change a people until they themselves desire change), so the world remained astray by its own choice.

Three words have no validity for the People of Truth: 'impossible' (everything is possible), 'innocent' (a child is in reality a sinner come to settle accounts), and 'accident' (every accident is in truth a predetermined event), since Allah is never unjust (ma kasabat aydikum).

Both 'we are architects of our fate' and 'fate goes where it wills' are true: in the world of intentions (alam-e-niyyat) we made our intentions, frozen in the record; in the world of action (alam-e-amal) we reap them (jabr) while also acting freely (ikhtiyar/tadbir).
Ali explained jabr and ikhtiyar to a Bedouin by having him lift one foot (ikhtiyar) then being unable to lift the other (jabr), showing how much is free will and how much is compulsion.

In the realm of jabr Allah appointed the angels (mudabbirat amra) to ensure each predetermined event occurs; in the realm of ikhtiyar He sends the Book and the messenger (da'iyan ila Allahi bi-idhnihi) to guide us; supplication (du'a) is the eraser that averts qada and bala.

Du'a is more excellent than reciting the Quran because Allah loves the words of our humility (nadamah) more; though du'a averts fate, an unaccepted du'a is stored as reward for the day of death/Qiyamat, the most needed provision.

Life is like two joined tape recorders: one reel unwinds (the intentions made before, now reaped as jabr, the echo of the dome), while one fills (the intentions made now, to be heard/reaped in the coming life), so one must fill with understanding through worship.

Surah al-Hamd (al-Fatiha) is the divine model of supplication: first praise (tahmid) of Allah, then the request (ihdina al-sirat al-mustaqim), then seeking refuge from the misguided; the du'as of Imam Zayn al-Abidin and Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq complete what we do not know to ask.

Shafa'at (intercession) means grace marks/joining for a small shortfall, not a license to sin; Muslims corrupted it by softening hell and embellishing paradise, and fabricated hadiths (e.g. Abu Hurayrah, Shimr as narrators) such as Abu Bakr and Umar being elders of paradise, though there are no old people in paradise.

There are two paradises: a spiritual paradise for the soul (merging into the haykal with the Imam, residing in the tenth barzakh above the Ka'ba until the Qa'im releases all haykals) and a physical paradise for the tempered body, both beginning from the grave; khalidin means one grand epoch (kaur-e-azam), not literal eternity.

The Sulaymanis, having endured hardship in the era of the Qa'im, will be the first to manifest in the daur-e-kashf, an era with no disease, mosquitoes, or legal restrictions, the Hazir Imam present, with tay al-ard (folding of the earth under one's step) when the body becomes equal to the soul.

The Imam currently resides in the Great Sahara at a place called Jabarsa (Jabalsa), unreachable, guarded by a deadly fly and Allah's land/sea/air forces, where countless believers (and some sent by the manasib like Fazal Ali and Yasin) are present.

The unbeliever's punishment proceeds: torment of the grave, then the seven darakat (Abyssinians, monkey/bear, predators, insects, birds, plants, minerals = Azab-e-Adna), then the poles (Azab-e-Araf, in huge animal forms in snow), then Saqar (Azab-e-Saqra), the latter two only for those the Qa'im sentences to hell.

Saqar (hell) is an inverted pot made of explosive materials (sulfur, gunpowder, lime, potash) with 70 valleys; the damned are given abnormal multi-headed multi-armed bodies (the source of temple idols and the art of Ellora-Ajanta), neither dying nor living (la yamutuna fiha wa la yahya), burned by the moon's light by day and the sun's by night.

Iblis (Harith bin Murra) will be the first standard-bearer made to enter hell, his satanic progeny following; all the damned must complete the duration of a grand epoch (kaur-e-azam) then re-enter the cycle as mineral, plant, animal and human to be offered the da'wat again.

We await the Mahdi (whose coming is sudden, inna al-sa'ata aatiyatun baghtatan), who will come before the Qa'im on the front of the Prophet (the son of the Abdullah-equivalent), while the Qa'im (whose time is known and fixed) will establish the Resurrection on the front of Ali (the son of the Abu-Talib-equivalent).
